title: Machine-Checked Exact-Rational Dissimilarity, Binary-Counter, and Superpolynomial Space-Lower-Bound Certificates for Polynomial-Time Quantum Computation
abstract: A. C. Cem Say (arXiv:2611.32633, November 24, 2026) established unconditional space lower bounds for polynomial-time bounded-error quantum Turing machines (QTMs), proving that two-way quantum finite automata (2QCFAs) are strictly weaker than o(log log n)-space polynomial-time QTMs (Theorem 2, via Z^k word-problem dissimilarity) and uncovering an infinite hierarchy of languages L_i separating sublogarithmic space classes Omega(log n / (log log n)^i) (Theorem 3, via binary-counter two-track palindromes and a double-exponential runtime-vs.-space barrier). We present a machine-checked, zero-floating-point formalization and certificate auditing framework for the finite combinatorial, algebraic, and inequality core of these separations. An 18-theorem zero-dependency Lean 4 kernel (Lean 4.35.0; 0 sorry, 0 warnings, 0 Classical.choice, 1 zero-axiom theorem) certifies arbitrary-dimension Z^k cancellation and dissimilarity (Fin k -> Int), unary encoding length <= (k+2)n, exact 1D/2D/3D L1-ball bounds, polynomial-degree domination c*n^u < n^k, Remscrim's 2QCFA parameter u = c(2r)^4 d^2 >= 16, L_S binary-counter monotonicity, exact palindrome prefix separation on List Bool, Lemma 17 space-gap halving, and double-exponential vs. polynomial-degree dominance. A pure-stdlib zero-float verifier audits QUANTUM-SPACE-LB-CERT-1.0 across four modes, replaying 16 canonical certificates in 0.013-4.440 ms, passing brute-force Z^k L1-ball, unary-injectivity, and L_S/L_i cross-checks, and rejecting 57/57 live adversarial forgeries.
